item.title: Road closures for the week of February 28 – March 6
item.description: LIHUE — A number of road-related projects are on tap in the days ahead with grass cutting, tree trimming and guardrail repair making up the bulk of the work, the Hawaii Department of Transportation said in an update on Friday.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Navy must engage on Red Hill issues
item.description: Little more than fours years after the disastrous 2021 Red Hill fuel spill, the Navy has officially flicked off Oahu citizens who are asking questions it can’t or doesn’t want to answer about ongoing issues over the fuel facility’s closure, remediation and drinking water safety. item.title: Poll: Just one in four Americans supports U.S. strikes on Iran
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Only one in four Americans approves of the U.S. strikes that killed Iran’s leader, while about half — including one in four Republicans — believe President Donald Trump is too willing to use military force, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that concluded on Sunday.

item.title: Happy Camper for Monday, March 2, 2026
item.description: Jean Souza and the volunteers at the Kauai Ocean Discovery Center were busy distributing the newly published kohola, or humpback whale, educational posters during the Mahina Olelo Hawaii event (February is Native Hawaiian Language Month), Ola Ka ‘i Kauai Niihau (“the language thrives”) at the Kukui Grove Center.

item.title: Strong January masks Hawaii’s uneven tourism outlook
item.description: Hawaii opened 2026 with its strongest January since the pandemic, but the University of Hawaii Economic Research Organization’s new first‑quarter forecast underscores how uneven the tourism economy remains despite the strong gains.

item.title: Healthy Living Spring Celebration
item.description: The 3rd annual Healthy Living Spring Celebration was held at the Samuel Mahelona Memorial Hospital in Kapaa on Saturday, hosted by Hawaii News Now’s Dillon Encheta.

item.title: Celebrating ‘Olelo Hawaii: The Native Hawaiian Language is thriving on Kauai and Niihau
item.description: February is recognized as Mahina ‘Olelo Hawaii, or “Hawaiian Language Month,” and Kauai joined the statewide celebrations and festivities.

item.title: Kauai sees more whales during recent count
item.description: LIHUE — For the second time this year, 487 volunteers collected data on kohola, or humpback whales, from the shores of Kauai, Oahu, Molokai and Hawaii Island during the Hawaiian Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary Ocean Count on Saturday.
